utility.notes: Silicon Valley Power is the City of Santa Clara's own municipal electric utility, serving Santa Clara since 1896 and delivering 100% carbon-free power to residential customers. Santa Clara is not served by PG&E for electric delivery.

value.name: Silicon Valley Power (SVP)
value.notes: SVP is a vertically-integrated municipal utility (like Palo Alto's CPAU, Riverside Public Utilities, Burbank Water and Power, and Glendale Water and Power) — it generates/procures and delivers its own power rather than sitting alongside a separate CCA. Santa Clara is notably absent from Silicon Valley Clean Energy's 13-community member list, consistent with Santa Clara having its own municipal utility rather than being PG&E/SVCE territory.

permit_authority.value: City of Santa Clara Community Development Department, Building Division

interconnection_url.notes: SVP's own utility rules and regulations page, hosting NEM/interconnection rules.

value.name: Battery Storage Rebate
value.description: SVP's own residential battery storage rebate, listed under its Solar & Battery rebate category. $0.15 per watt-hour of installed capacity, up to a maximum of $2,700. Income-qualified customers may receive additional bonus incentives of $2,000 (Financial Rate Assistance Program) and $2,000 (LIHEAP), for a combined maximum of up to $6,700.
value.eligibility: City of Santa Clara residents receiving electricity from Silicon Valley Power. Income-qualified customers enrolled in the Financial Rate Assistance Program or meeting LIHEAP income requirements are eligible for additional bonus incentives.

value.name: Silicon Valley Power (SVP) Interconnection Agreement Pre-Approval Letter
value.required_when: always (must be obtained before SolarAPP+ registration)

value.name: SolarAPP+ Approval Document
value.required_when: SolarAPP+-eligible projects (licensed contractors only, systems up to 15 kW, energy storage no more than 1 battery / 20 kWh)

value.notes: Search-engine synthesis of the city's own page indicates the Building Division reviews and approves SolarAPP+ permits within 1-2 business days in most cases; not independently confirmed via direct fetch this session.
